questions.question: What is the role of acyl Co A dehydrogenase enzyme in oxidation of palmitate? a). oxidation b). Reduction c). transesterification d). hydration / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Small Intestine (Major Site):
  • The small intestine is the principal site for lipid digestion. When partially
  • digested fat enters the duodenum, it stimulates the release of bile and
  • pancreatic juice, which are essential for effective fat digestion.
  • Role of Bile:
  • Bile is produced by the liver and stored in the gallbladder. It contains bile salts
  • that emulsify fats, breaking large fat globules into tiny droplets. Emulsification
  • increases the surface area of fats, making them more accessible to digestive
  • enzymes. Bile salts also help in the formation of micelles later during
  • absorption.
  • Pancreatic Enzymes:
  • The pancreas secretes several enzymes into the small intestine:
  • Pancreatic lipase is the most important enzyme and converts triglycerides into
  • 2-monoglycerides and free fatty acids. Its activity is aided by colipase.
  • Phospholipase A ₂ digests phospholipids into lysophospholipids and fatty
  • acids.
  • Cholesterol esterase hydrolyzes cholesterol esters into free cholesterol and
  • fatty acids.
  • End Products:
  • The digestion of lipids in the small intestine produces free fatty acids,
  • monoglycerides, cholesterol, and lysophospholipids, which are then ready
  • to be absorbed by the intestinal mucosal cells. [U] / [CO3]

questions.question: Evaluate protein digestion and assess the role of brush-border peptidases in the final stages of protein digestion. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate protein digestion and assess the role of brush-border peptidases in the final stages
  • of protein digestion.
  • Protein digestion is the process by which dietary proteins are broken down into
  • amino acids so that they can be absorbed and used by the body. This process
  • begins in the stomach, where the acidic environment (hydrochloric acid)
  • denatures proteins and activates the e nzyme pepsin from its inactive form,
  • pepsinogen. Pepsin breaks proteins into smaller polypeptides.
  • In the small intestine, protein digestion continues with the help of pancreatic enzymes
  • such as trypsin, chymotrypsin, elastase, and carboxypeptidases, which further break
  • polypeptides into smaller peptides and amino acids.
  • intestinal peptidases present on the brush border of intestinal cells convert peptides
  • into free amino acids, dipeptides, and tripeptides. [E] / [CO1]

questions.question: Explain and illustrate why urine turns dark on standing in alkaptonuria. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain and illustrate why urine turns dark on standing in alkaptonuria.
  • Alkaptonuria is a rare inborn error of metabolism caused by a deficiency of the
  • enzyme homogentisic acid oxidase, which is involved in the metabolism of the
  • amino acids phenylalanine and tyrosine. Due to this enzyme defect,
  • homogentisic acid accumulates in the body and is excreted in the urine.
  • A characteristic feature of alkaptonuria is that the urine turns dark brown or black on
  • standing due to oxidation of homogentisic acid. [U] / [CO3]
